strings.name: Floyd Mayweather Jr.
strings.summary: Mayweather's defense, distance control and counterpunching brought world titles in five divisions and a 50–0 professional record. Fights with Pacquiao, De La Hoya and McGregor expanded pay-per-view and self-promotion models. Since 2017 he has mainly boxed exhibitions. His public record also includes a domestic-battery conviction and 2026 check-related criminal charges; the latter are allegations, not convictions.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: A world champion in multiple weight divisions whose competitive and business models influenced modern professional boxing.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.highlights.h1.title: Five-division world champion
strings.highlights.h1.text: Won major world titles from super-featherweight to light-middleweight.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and early training
strings.facts.f2.value: Trained by his father and uncle in a boxing family; attended Ottawa Hills High School.
strings.highlights.h2.title: 50–0 and commercial influence
strings.highlights.h2.text: Reached 50–0 in 2017; major pay-per-view fights and promotion shaped boxing business.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Announced future fight plans
strings.timeline.t1.text: Said he planned a December Bangkok exhibition; it had not occurred, nor had a professional comeback been completed.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Check-related charges
strings.timeline.t2.text: Nevada brought theft and check-fraud charges over a watch purchase; charges are not a conviction.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Boxing Hall of Fame ceremony
strings.timeline.t3.text: Attended the pandemic-delayed induction as a member of the 2021 class.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Defeated McGregor
strings.timeline.t4.text: Reached 50–0 professionally before turning to exhibitions.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Faced Pacquiao
strings.timeline.t5.text: Won a decision in the highly publicized welterweight title fight.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Served domestic-battery sentence
strings.timeline.t6.text: Jailed after a misdemeanor domestic-battery conviction; released after about two months.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Defeated De La Hoya
strings.timeline.t7.text: Won a light-middleweight title and expanded his pay-per-view reach.
strings.timeline.t8.title: First world championship
strings.timeline.t8.text: Beat Genaro Hernández for a super-featherweight title.
strings.timeline.t9.title: Olympic bronze and professional debut
strings.timeline.t9.text: Won Atlanta featherweight bronze and turned professional that year.
